name: Data Storytelling & Business Communication
description: Turning analysis into clear, audience-focused narratives and recommendations that drive business decisions.

questions.question: Before designing any chart for a presentation, what should you clarify first?
options: Which color palette to use
Which charting library is fastest
Who the audience is and what you want them to know or do
How many slides the deck should have
questions.explanation: Effective data stories start from the audience and the desired action; design choices follow from that.

questions.question: Which slide title communicates an insight rather than just a topic?
options: Q3 Revenue
Revenue by Region
Sales Data Overview
Q3 revenue grew 12%, driven by the North region
questions.explanation: An action/insight title states the takeaway, so the audience knows what the chart is meant to show.

questions.question: You want to draw attention to one line among six on a line chart. Which technique is most effective?
options: Color the key line in a strong color and gray out the others
Give each line a different bright color
Add a 3D effect to the chart
Increase the number of gridlines
questions.explanation: Using preattentive attributes such as color contrast against muted gray directs the viewer's eye to what matters.

questions.question: In an executive summary for busy stakeholders, where should the main recommendation usually appear?
options: In an appendix
At the beginning, before supporting detail
Only at the very end after all analysis
It should be left implicit for the audience to infer
questions.explanation: The 'bottom line up front' (pyramid principle) approach leads with the conclusion and then supports it.

questions.question: A bar chart's y-axis starts at 95 instead of 0, making a 2% difference look like a 3x difference. What is the main problem?
options: Bar charts cannot display percentages
The chart has too few categories
The colors are not accessible
Truncating the baseline of a bar chart exaggerates differences because bar length encodes value
questions.explanation: Bar length is read as magnitude, so bars should start at zero; truncated axes mislead.

questions.question: Your analysis shows stores with more staff have higher sales, and a manager wants to hire more staff everywhere. What is the most responsible way to communicate this?
options: State that the data shows a correlation, note possible confounders such as store size, and suggest a controlled test
Confirm that hiring more staff will increase sales
Omit the finding because it might be misinterpreted
Present only the stores that support the conclusion
questions.explanation: Correlation does not prove causation; a good communicator states limitations and proposes how to validate the causal claim.

practical.title: Write an insight summary for a manager
practical.instructions: Monthly churn rose from 3% in January to 5% in March. Most of the increase came from customers on the Basic plan after a price increase in February. Write 2-4 sentences for a non-technical manager that state the key insight with numbers, explain the likely cause, and give a clear recommendation.
practical.expected_output: A short summary such as: 'Churn rose from 3% to 5% between January and March, mostly among Basic plan customers after the February price increase. We recommend testing a discount or a lower-priced tier for Basic customers and monitoring churn over the next month.'

rubric.description: Quantifies the change with the numbers
rubric.hint: Include the actual figures (3% to 5%) so the change is concrete.
Name the segment driving the change (Basic plan customers).

rubric.description: Links the change to the price increase
rubric.hint: Explain the likely cause: the February price increase.
End with an actionable recommendation for the manager.

tasks.title: Study storytelling with data principles
tasks.description: Read several articles on the Storytelling with Data site about context, decluttering and focusing attention. Note the main principles you will apply.
tasks.completion_criteria: Written list of at least 5 principles with one example each.

tasks.title: Rewrite chart titles as insights
tasks.description: Take five charts from a public report or your own work and rewrite each topic title as a one-sentence insight title. Declutter one chart by removing unnecessary gridlines, borders and legends.
tasks.completion_criteria: Five before/after title pairs and one decluttered chart.

tasks.title: Build a three-slide data narrative
tasks.description: Analyze a Kaggle dataset and produce three slides: context, key insight with a focused chart, and recommendation. Use color only to highlight the main point.
tasks.completion_criteria: Three slides with insight titles and a recommendation, reviewed by one peer.

tasks.title: Present an end-to-end analysis to stakeholders
tasks.description: Run an analysis on a realistic business question, write a one-page executive memo with the recommendation up front, and deliver a 10-minute presentation. Address limitations and next steps.
tasks.completion_criteria: One-page memo, slide deck and recorded or live presentation with documented audience questions.
